subject: Re: Air-gapped private deployment — IaC review and GitOps handoff
messages:
From: Liam O'Connell <liam@acme-corp.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Cloud Ops <cloud-ops@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Air-gapped deployment: request for IaC review

Hi Grace —

Thanks for taking this. We're working toward a locked-down, air-gapped private deployment for the initial rollout of the Redwood stack in our on-prem datacenter. Before we sign off with procurement and networking, we need a focused review of the Terraform/Helm/Ansible artifacts and the GitOps pipeline to make sure:

- network segmentation (management vs. inference vs. tenant VLANs) is explicit in Terraform modules
- Helm charts are templated for an offline image registry and support imagePullSecrets
- Ansible playbooks include idempotent bootstrap steps and local CA handling
- CI runs security scans (Snyk) and fails fast on license or critical alerts

I've attached our current board-level IaC matrix and a rough airgap playbook. Can your team review and call out gaps? We have a hard freeze on 2027-05-02 for procurement readiness.

Appreciate a quick sanity pass and high-level notes — we can schedule a deep technical sync if needed.

Cheers,
Liam
Liam O'Connell
Head of Cloud Operations, Acme Corp.
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connell <liam@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-10T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment: request for IaC review

Liam —

Thanks for the context and the attachments. Quick high-level take from our side so you have initial expectations before a deeper pass:

- Terraform: good separation of network boundaries, but we want explicit egress stub resources and a CIDR allowlist module for management plane traffic; also, ensure module outputs do not leak sensitive hostnames (use data objects).
- Helm: chart values already allow repository override; need a documented offline registry bootstrap (tarball import + local harbor config). We'll add a values schema that forbids imagePullPolicy: Always in airgapped mode.
- Ansible: bootstrap looks fine; convert the CA steps into a role that checks for existing certs and backs them up to /opt/redwood/certs. Add --check dry-run to reconcile playbooks in CI.
- CI/GitOps: require Snyk SBOM generation and fail on high/critical; add a gating PR job that runs validator (terraform validate + tflint) and helm unit tests (ct).

We can do a 60m technical sync tomorrow morning PT if that works. I've asked Jasmine to run a targeted diff against our canonical private-deploy modules and produce a short patch list.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Staff Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connell <liam@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T08:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment: request for IaC review

Attaching a short set of diffs and the 'gitops-policy-diff.patch' — summary below. I pulled the Acme repo and compared against our modules:

1) terraform/modules/networking: add resource "aws_network_acl" equivalent for on-prem (firewall_rules.tf) to ensure management subnet cannot create outbound 0.0.0.0/0 rules. (Patch included.)
2) terraform/modules/egress: replace hard-coded monitored CIDRs with an input list plus an allowlist validation (pre-commit check).
3) helm/charts/redwood-core: add 'offline.registry.enabled' boolean; when true, chart renders imagePullSecrets and local image paths. Also: add --set strictImagePolicy=true note in README.
4) ansible/roles/bootstrap/tasks/main.yml: idempotency check for CA cert bootstrap and a fallback to 'generate-local-ca: false' if a customer-managed CA is present.
5) ci/.github/workflows/priv-gate.yml: add step to run 'snyk test --severity-threshold=high' and upload SBOM to artifact store; mark job as required in branch protection for 'main'.

I flagged a couple of items in the patch that need decisions:
- whether we allow a 'management egress proxy' as an exception (tends to be necessary for apt/yum updates in very locked environments)
- how we represent image digests vs tags in the Helm values (recommend digest-only for production airgapped catalogs)

I'll be on tomorrow's sync with a demo of the patch application (local apply against a mocked network).

-- Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Principal Software Engineer, Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: gitops-policy-diff.patch
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connell <liam@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T10:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment: request for IaC review

Thanks — a couple of compliance/security notes from the SOC 2 perspective before we lock the modules:

- Audit logging: make sure that all Terraform applies produce an operation log (who/what/when) and that the GitOps operator does not run with a blanket cluster-admin token. Recommend using a short-lived service account (KSA with OIDC) per cluster and capture apply events to an append-only audit S3 (or on-prem equivalent).
- Secrets handling: in airgapped mode, our docs currently recommend Vault; confirm that secret_backend: vault is plumbed through Helm values and Ansible roles do not write secrets to /tmp.
- Vulnerability policy: in addition to Snyk, add an allowlist for distro packages that need exceptions during freeze windows; require documented approvals in a linked Jira ticket.

Action items I want captured in the sync:
1) Define one acceptable management egress pattern (proxy vs scheduled updates).
2) Confirm Vault integration for secrets (or document alternative: HSM/KMS with offline syncing).
3) Make the CI gating policy required in branch protection for the Acme repo.

Soojin
Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connell <liam@acme-corp.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-12T15:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment: request for IaC review — sync notes and next steps

Team —

Thanks everyone for the fast turnaround. Notes from today's 60m sync + agreed next steps:

Summary of decisions:
- Management egress: Acme will adopt a scheduled egress window with an authenticated proxy; Redwood to provide an example proxy module and a runbook for scheduled updates.
- Image handling: production airgap mode will require image digest pinning; Helm charts updated to accept digest-only values.
- Secrets: Vault will be the standard; Redwood will update Helm values and Ansible roles to ensure Vault pathing and tokenless bootstrap via KMS-wrapped initial secrets (documented in airgap-playbook.md).
- CI gating: Snyk SBOM + tflint + helm-ct tests must pass; Acme will enable branch protection with the required checks.

Action items and owners:
- Jasmine: raise PR to redwood-inference/priv-deploy with the patch set and the README changes (due 2027-04-15) — attachment: gitops-policy-diff.patch
- Grace: produce 'management-egress-proxy' terraform module and example runbook (due 2027-04-19) — attachment: airgap-playbook.md
- Soojin: draft compliance exceptions process and Jira template (JIRA: IAC-7832) (due 2027-04-16)
- Liam/Acme: enable branch protection and confirm your offline registry onboarding plan by 2027-04-22

Attachments bundled: iac-review-matrix.xlsx (detailed mapping), airgap-playbook.md (runbook draft), gitops-policy-diff.patch

If there are no blockers, we'll treat these as the canonical follow-ups and pick up the PR reviews when Jasmine opens them.

Best,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Staff Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
